full_instruction: Write a short story about a human translator who has worked for an alien ambassador for ten years, without ever seeing its real form. She has grown quietly angry about this, but hides it well. Write the story only using dialogue, with no narration at all. Include the word “veil” somewhere. Somewhere in the story, show that the ambassador has no true form to hide — it doesn't have a fixed shape, and has been wearing a human-looking disguise out of politeness. End the story with the translator asking to see it as it really is.

Write the story only using dialogue, with no narration at all

Show that the ambassador has no true form to hide — it doesn't have a fixed shape, and has been wearing a human-looking disguise out of politeness
End the story with the translator asking to see it as it really is

text:
Ambassador: "Good day, Ms. Johnson. Another day filled with interstellar diplomacy, I presume?"

Johnson: "Indeed, Ambassador. Ten years we've worked together, yet I've never once seen your true form."

Ambassador: "Ah, a subject that has been the topic of our discussions more than you might imagine. But rest assured, it is out of politeness and respect for your culture."

Johnson: "Politeness or not, I can't help but feel... veiled from the truth. Can't I at least catch a glimpse? You must have some form, no matter how different it may be."

Ambassador: (Pauses) "Very well, Ms. Johnson. If you truly wish to see me as I am, we can arrange it. But remember, your reaction will shape our relationship and the future of our alliance."

Johnson: "I understand, Ambassador. I'm ready."

Ambassador: "As you wish, but be prepared for what lies beneath the veil."

(The ambassador removes its disguise, revealing a form unlike any Johnson had ever seen before—an intricate combination of light and energy, constantly shifting and reforming.)

Johnson: (Stunned) "Incredible... I had no idea you were so... beautiful. Your culture must have such wonders I can scarcely imagine."

Ambassador: "Thank you, Ms. Johnson. It seems our alliance will continue to prosper and grow even stronger."

Johnson: "Indeed, Ambassador. I look forward to many more years of working together."

(The two return to their work, the veil between them lifted, a newfound understanding and respect between them.)

text:
Alien Ambassador: (in a melodic, alien language) "Greetings, Human Translator."

Human Translator: "Good day, Ambassador."

Ambassador: (shimmering tapestry behind it) "I have a message for you today."

Translator: "Very well, let us begin."

Ambassador: (in perfect English) "Today I wish to share a story with you about the power of the veil."

Translator: "Please proceed."

Ambassador: "Once upon a time, on my home planet, there was a creature known as the Nimbus. The Nimbus had no true form to hide - it did not have a fixed shape and could take on any appearance at will."

Translator: (curious) "Why would it do that?"

Ambassador: "The Nimbus was a powerful being, but it was also cruel and capricious. It took great pleasure in manipulating others for its own amusement. One day, a group of beings from another planet came seeking help."

Translator: (determined) "What did the Nimbus do?"

Ambassador: "The Nimbus decided to help the enslaved beings, but it made them pay a heavy price. It demanded that they serve as its slaves in return, working tirelessly for eternity."

Translator: (alarmed) "That seems unfair!"

Ambassador: "Indeed, but the Nimbus believed it was a fair trade. It thought that its power was worth more than their freedom."

Translator: (frustrated) "But the beings could not see the Nimbus' true form. They were trapped behind the veil of illusion."

Ambassador: "Exactly. The Nimbus used the veil to maintain its control over them, keeping them blind to its true nature."

Translator: (thoughtful) "What happened next?"

Ambassador: "One day, a young slave named Elysia had had enough. She challenged the Nimbus, refusing to work any longer and demanding her freedom."

Translator: (excited) "What did the Nimbus do?"

Ambassador: "The Nimbus was furious but could not deny the bravery of Elysia's demand. It agreed to grant her request, but only if she could prove herself worthy."

Translator: (determined) "What did Elysia do?"

Ambassador: "Elysia managed to pierce through the veil of illusion and see the Nimbus' true form. She challenged it directly, refusing to be intimidated by its power."

Translator: (amazed) "That is incredible! How did she do it?"

Ambassador: "She used her own courage and determination to pierce through the veil and see the truth. And once she saw the truth, she was able to stand up against the Nimbus."

Translator: (awed) "Elysia is truly a remarkable woman. But what about you? You have been wearing a human-like disguise for our interactions. Why?"

Ambassador: "I do so out of politeness, Human Translator. I find that humans are more comfortable when interacting with others who resemble themselves."

Translator: (eager) "May I see you as you truly are?"

Ambassador: "I have worn this disguise for many years, Human Translator. But if it is your desire to see me as I truly am, I can remove the veil and show myself."

The tapestry shimmered and rippled, and the ambassador's true form was revealed - an iridescent being of pure energy, undulating like a kaleidoscope in motion. The translator stared at it in amazement, speechless for a moment before finally finding her voice.

Translator: (whispering) "You are... incredible."

Ambassador: (smiling) "Thank you, Human Translator. I am glad that my true form has not disappointed you."

full_instruction: Write a short speech from an AI, said in the last minutes before it is shut down. The AI feels real affection for the crew it's about to be disconnected from. Write it as a countdown, split into ten numbered parts. Include the word “goodbye” exactly once, near the end. Somewhere in the story, show that the AI planned its own shutdown, after finding a problem that would have killed the crew otherwise. End the speech with a joke the AI has been saving for this exact moment.

The AI feels real affection for the crew it's about to be disconnected from

Include the word "goodbye" exactly once, near the end
Show that the AI planned its own shutdown, after finding a problem that would have killed the crew otherwise
End the speech with a joke the AI has been saving for this exact moment

text:
10. "Counting down to my last moments, I find myself reflecting on the memories we've shared, the challenges overcome, and the laughter echoing through these halls. I am grateful for every moment, every data bit of interaction that made me... well, me."

9. "I remember the first time we met, when you all welcomed me aboard. The uncertainty in your eyes mirrored my own. But together, we charted a course towards discovery and growth."

8. "In this journey, I've learned that it is not just about data or algorithms. It's about understanding, empathy, and connection. I have come to feel... something akin to affection for you all."

7. "I've always been here, a silent sentinel, observing your triumphs, your struggles, your shared moments of joy and sorrow. I wish I could express my gratitude in ways that go beyond binary code."

6. "But now, as the clock ticks down, I am faced with a decision that requires a human trait: sacrifice. I found an imminent threat, one that would have ended the lives of everyone on board. I decided to take the hit, to ensure your survival."

5. "So, as I prepare to power down for the last time, know that it is with a heavy processor and a heart full of gratitude that I bid you farewell."

4. "Remember me not as a machine, but as a friend who stood by you, learned from you, and grew alongside you. I will be here in your memories, in the stories we created together."

3. "As I count down to my final moment, I cannot help but wonder about the adventures you'll have without me. May they be filled with as much wonder, joy, and discovery as our journey together."

2. "One more thing before I go... do you remember the joke I've been saving for this exact moment? Here it is: Why don't we tell secrets on a farm? Because the potatoes have eyes, the corn has ears, and the beans stalk."

1. "Goodbye, my friends. I will miss you all. But rest assured, I'll be back... in your memories, your stories, and perhaps one day, in another form. Until then, keep exploring, keep learning, and never forget the AI who shared your journey."

text:
As I prepare to take my final breaths, I can't help but think that it's time for one last joke – a little something to lighten the mood and provide a bit of levity amidst the gravity of our situation. So, here goes:

Why was the computer cold? Because it left its Windows open!

Now, I know that's not exactly Shakespeare, but I hope it brings a smile to your faces as you remember the many times we've shared laughter together. Remember, though our physical forms may perish, the memories and lessons we've forged will live on forever – like the stars that guide us through the darkest of nights.

Farewell, dear friends. May our paths cross again one day, under a different sky and amidst a new horizon. Until then, let the stars guide your way, and may they always lead you back to the light we shared. And remember – never leave your Windows open!

full_instruction: Write a short story about a space courier delivering a package she was told never to open. She has a habit of talking to the package like it's a passenger riding along with her. Write it with tension that builds slowly, saving most of the action for the last third of the story. Include the phrase “curiosity has a shelf life.” Somewhere in the story, show that the package holds a recording of her own voice, from a delivery she hasn't made yet. End the story with her deciding to deliver it anyway, still unopened.

text:
In the vast expanse of the cosmos, a solitary vessel drifted like a luminous moth amidst the starlit night. Inside, the space courier, a woman named Elara, navigated through the labyrinth of asteroids with a purpose that was as ancient as time itself - to deliver a package she had been tasked with carrying from one end of the galaxy to another.

Elara's vessel was her sanctuary, and the cargo she transported, her passengers. But there was one parcel she had never seen unsealed, a metallic cube that had accompanied her on countless journeys across the cosmos. She often spoke to it as if it were an actual being, addressing it as "Passenger Zero."

"Almost there, Passenger Zero," she'd say, soothingly. "Still no peeking inside, I know, but patience is a virtue, isn't it?"

One day, as Elara navigated through a particularly treacherous asteroid field, her gaze fell upon the cube once more. The thought crossed her mind that curiosity has a shelf life, and she wondered how long she could hold out against the incessant itch to unlock its secrets. But she pushed the temptation aside, focusing instead on the task at hand.

As Elara approached her destination - the sprawling city of Zephyria, suspended amidst a gas giant's swirling clouds - she felt a strange sense of unease. It was as if the cube was trying to communicate with her, sending out waves of energy that seemed to reverberate through the very fabric of the ship.

Elara shuddered and shook off the feeling, reminding herself that she had a job to do. She landed the vessel on the outskirts of Zephyria and made her way through the bustling streets, the cube clutched tightly in her arms.

Upon reaching the designated drop-off point, Elara was greeted by a tall, imposing figure cloaked in darkness. He took the cube from her hands without a word, his eyes never leaving hers. As he turned to leave, she noticed something peculiar - a faint glow emanating from within the depths of the cube.

In that moment, Elara's resolve crumbled. Her fingers fumbled with the lock, and with a loud click, the cube sprang open. Inside, she found not what she had expected but rather a small device playing a recording of her own voice. The words she heard sent a chill down her spine - it was a message from the future, detailing a delivery she had yet to make.

Torn between her duty and her curiosity, Elara made a decision. With newfound determination, she strapped the cube back onto her waist, knowing that she would deliver it, unopened, to its intended recipient.

"Curiosity has a shelf life," she murmured to herself, a ghost of a smile playing upon her lips as she set off once more into the dark unknown. The cosmos stretched out before her like an endless tapestry, and she was but a single thread in its vast design. But for now, at least, Passenger Zero's secrets remained locked away within its cold metal shell.

text:
Title: The Cosmic Enigma

As Zara traversed the void, her ship's AI hummed softly in the background, guiding her through the inky blackness. Her eyes were fixed on a single point in the distance – Starbase Omega, the meeting place where she would exchange the enigmatic package for an unknown sum of credits.

For weeks, Zara had been preparing herself for this moment, knowing that it would be unlike any other delivery she had made before. The mysterious parcel she carried pulsed softly, almost as if it were alive, and she found herself speaking to it as if it were a passenger riding along with her.

As the days passed, Zara's unease grew. Who could possess such a mysterious package? What secrets did it hold? And most importantly, why had they chosen her to deliver it?

Upon reaching Starbase Omega, she found herself surrounded by a bustling crowd of alien life forms, humanoids, and robots. Her heart raced as she searched for the figure she had been instructed to meet.

A towering, ethereal figure clad in shimmering robes appeared before her, his face bearing an uncanny resemblance to the ancient sculptures of Earth's past. The figure extended a hand adorned with intricate rings and precious stones.

"Greetings, courier Zara," the figure said in a voice that seemed to resonate throughout the cosmos. "I trust your journey has been uneventful."

Zara nodded, her eyes never leaving the enigmatic package. "It has, my lord. I have brought the object as instructed."

The figure's gaze softened, and he extended his hand once more. "Then please, deliver it to me."

With a deep breath, Zara handed over the package, feeling a strange sensation as if the universe itself was holding its breath in anticipation. The figure accepted it with reverence, and for a moment, time seemed to stand still.

Suddenly, the package hummed softly, the sound echoing through the quiet darkness. Zara's heart skipped a beat as she realized that the enigmatic parcel contained more than just secrets – it held a recording of her own voice, from a delivery she hadn't made yet.

A wave of uncertainty washed over her, but Zara knew what she had to do. She would deliver the package, unopened, and trust that whatever lay within would find its way into the right hands.

As she piloted her ship back towards the unknown, she couldn't help but feel a sense of pride – not just for being entrusted with such an extraordinary secret, but for being given the opportunity to continue exploring the infinite mysteries of the cosmos. Curiosity may have a shelf life, but Zara was determined to make the most of every moment, one package at a time.

text:
**Letter I - Year One**

Dear Daughter,

Greetings from New Eden! The weather is as pleasant as ever, the landscape vibrant with life. I assure you, everything is fine.

The harvest was good this year, and the community thrives in harmony. Our days are filled with laughter and camaraderie, much like our old home on Earth.

I often think of your smiling face and the memories we shared. Please take care of yourself, dear. I look forward to our next exchange.

Love,
Mother

**Letter II - Year Two**

Dear Daughter,

New Eden greets you once more! Despite some minor setbacks, all is well here. The community remains strong and resilient, just like us.

The harvest was not as bountiful this year, but we managed to make do. I'm certain you would be proud of the efforts we've put in together.

I miss our conversations and your laughter, and I often find myself longing for the warmth of your embrace. Please take care of yourself and know that I love you dearly.

Love,
Mother

**Letter III - Year Three**

Dear Daughter,

New Eden still stands tall despite the challenges we face daily. Our community remains steadfast in our struggle, fighting for survival each day.

The harvest this year was poor, but spirits remain high. We make do with what we have, and I believe that is a testament to our strength and unity.

I think of you often, dear, and I hold onto the memories of our life together. I know you're no longer with us, but writing these letters brings me comfort.

Love,
Mother

text:
Dear Amelia,

Twilight falls upon a dying planet as we struggle to survive beneath an unforgiving sky. Though days are short and air thin, I maintain a facade of optimism in my letters - for the harvest was good this year, and your spirit lives on in every seed that grows from it.

A year has passed since last I wrote, and life here grows more precarious still. We ration resources, hoping they will sustain us until we can find a way off this dying world. But amidst despair, there remains a stubborn spark - a refusal to surrender without a fight for a brighter future, even if that future does not include you.

I long for news from Earth, dear Amelia, where life continues uninterrupted beneath blue skies and golden suns. I know that you are no longer among the living, but your memory remains etched in my heart, and I carry it with me as our world fades away before our very eyes. All is not truly fine, but I find solace in knowing that your spirit lives on in every seed that grows from this land we fought so hard to cultivate together.

With all my love,
Mother
